weekly_digest.narrative: 本周尚未结束（6/7 天）日均 162 条。合并 126 条、关闭 201 条。领域分布：推理 607、训练 297、方向 1、通用 68。热点主题：CUDA/Kernel (263)、Attention (153)、GRPO/PPO (146)。
weekly_digest.coverage_note: 快照覆盖不均：Megatron-LM、TensorRT-LLM、sglang、vllm 不足 7 天，总量与仓库排名仅供趋势参考

focus: sglang 本周通过让对端直接在尾核中读取对方部分和，消除了 TP2 diffusion 后行并行 GEMM 的冗余 NVLink all-reduce 通信。
vllm 为 ROCm 上的 TP+SP MoE 场景新增复制专家选项，可将跨卡集体通信量减半，显著优化大 MoE 模型推理吞吐。
TensorRT-LLM 与 sglang 推进 INT8 KV cache 的多 block 支持，使单内核启动在 96k 上下文场景下提速 7.6×，直接释放长序列推理性能瓶颈。
Quark W4A4 gpt-oss MoE 在 Blackwell 因缺失 CUTLASS 后端分支无法加载，且内核静默截断精度，存在上线崩溃与精度退化的双重风险。

modules.name: CUDA/Kernel
modules.note: INT8 KV cache 多 block 支持落地，使单 XQA 内核在 96k 上下文下提速 7.6×，释放长序列推理性能瓶颈。

modules.name: Attention
modules.note: vllm 启用 ROCM_RDNA_ATTN 作为 RDNA 3.x 默认注意力后端，覆盖 gfx1150–gfx1153 及新增 RDNA4 硬件支持。

modules.name: Quantization
modules.note: Quark W4A4 在 Blackwell 上因缺少 CUTLASS 分支导致加载失败且静默丢精度，亟需补齐后端适配。

modules.name: MoE
modules.note: vllm 新增 --enable-hc-sp-replicated-moe 标志，使 MoE 专家在 TP+SP 下按 rank 复制，减少一半跨卡通信。

modules.name: KV-Cache
modules.note: rocm_rdna_attn 被移植并设为 RDNA 3.x 默认后端，扩展了对 gfx115x/gfx1200 等 RDNA4 芯片的支持。

key_prs.why: 消除 TP2 diffusion 后冗余 NVLink all-reduce，大幅降低多卡通信开销，提升多机训练吞吐。
ROCm 上大 MoE 模型跨卡通信量减半，直接影响多卡推理延迟与带宽利用率。
将 RDNA 3.x/4.x 设为默认后端扩大了 AMD 推理硬件覆盖，但未经验证的显卡可能出现性能回退。
修复混合 MTP 推理时 Mamba 状态静默损坏与断言失败，避免线上模型输出错误结果。

## Motivation

With HiCache `write_back`, the device eviction walk backs its victims up to host and then blocks the scheduler on `Event.synchronize()` for those D2H copies before it demotes the victims. The copies are fenced behind the in-flight forward (`write_fence_stream`), so on a busy prefill server the scheduler cannot finish building the next batch until the current forward ends. On DSv4.1-Flash disaggregated prefill this wait was 50-56% of scheduler time, and the GPU sat idle while the next batch was prepared and launched.

## Motivation

With DP attention on a PD decode server, every DP rank's decode step lasts as long as the busiest rank's: ranks pad to the largest batch for the MoE/collective phase. Requests are placed on DP ranks when they arrive, but the per-rank running counts still drift apart as requests finish at different times. On DSv4.1-Flash with DEP16 decode, the busiest rank runs about 1.22x the mean, so every step pays for lanes that most ranks do not have.

items.title: [Spec Decode] Per-position acceptance rate over the drafts that reached each position
items.author: LantaoJin
items.summary: Fixes per-position acceptance rate in speculative decoding to divide by drafted tokens reaching each position instead of total drafts, correcting under-reported metrics under dynamic speculative decoding.
items.body:
## Overview

The per-position acceptance rate divides the accepted tokens at position `i` by the number of drafts. When drafts are shorter than `num_speculative_tokens`, for example under dynamic speculative decoding, that under-reports every later position, and a position no draft reached shows `0.000`. This PR divides by the drafted tokens at each position everywhere the rate is computed, and exports the counter that makes it computable from `/metrics`. A second commit seeds the dummy prompts of `vllm bench latency`, whose run-to-run variance hid this kind of change in A/B runs.

Follow-up
discussion: Documentation preview: https://vllm--67610.org.readthedocs.build/en/67610/

cc @tomasruizt since this follows up #64156 and mirrors its per-position verified counter. With dynamic SD on a real engine, positions 1–2 were reported about 6x low before this change (0.071 vs 0.451, see Validation).

### What does this PR do?

The torch backend of `FusedLinearForPPO` (the default fused backend) divides the bf16 logits by the temperature before upcasting to fp32, so log-probs differ from the rollout sampler’s formula (fp32 logits / T) by up to 0.054 at T=0.7, and the returned entropy is bf16. ## Motivation

`DetokenizeState.step` only commits text and advances `surr_offset`/`read_offset` when the new text is non-empty and does not end with U+FFFD. items.body:

## Overview

Online quantization loads each layer into a short-lived BF16 buffer and runs the layer's existing `process_weights_after_loading` (PWAL) when its last shard arrives. Cold start and weight updates share that path. Direct weight reload (`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`) now supports online-quantized models, and online quantization no longer uses the layerwise reload machinery. Part of the direct weight reload RFC (#54477). This supersedes #65802 (same author), which staged online layers through the layerwise machinery, so it doesn't duplicate an open PR.

items.title: [ROCm][Perf][Qwen4Exp] Add --enable-hc-sp-replicated-moe
items.author: eppaneamd
items.summary: Adds an opt-in flag to keep MoE experts replicated per rank under TP+sequence-parallelism on ROCm, halving inter-rank collectives per decoder layer at the cost of ~24 GiB extra weight memory.
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

With TP=2 and `--enable-hc-sp`, each ROCm Qwen4Exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) decoder layer all-gathers the MoE input and reduce-scatters its output around TP-sharded experts.

The opt-in `--enable-hc-sp-replicated-moe` (off by default) keeps every routed expert and the fused shared expert whole on each rank. The MoE then runs on the rank's own sequence-parallel rows, so those two collectives per layer go away. The attention keeps its all-gather and reduce-scatter.

ModelSlim W4A8 MoE initializes its scheme without a TP-size argument, leaving the default at 1. In the historical A3 test this configuration produced 0/64 correct GSM8K answers, all truncated.

items.body:
## Motivation

With DP (`--dp-size`) or DP attention (`--attn-dp-size`), each DP rank has its own radix cache, so a request only hits the cache if it lands on the rank that already served its prefix. The in-process `DataParallelController` never looks at the prompt: `auto` resolves to `round_robin`, and `total_requests` / `total_tokens` only look at load. So turns of the same multi-turn session land on arbitrary ranks, and each rank re-prefills the history. Under DP attention this hurts every rank, because the MoE layers run in lockstep and wait for the slowest rank's prefill.

items.title: [Fix] marlin: Load dense group scales and zero points at group boundaries
items.author: JonSnow1807
items.summary: With an FP8 block-quantized checkpoint, the dense Marlin kernel intermittently returns wrong GEMM results, which shows up as wrong greedy tokens. When a 128-wide group spans two 64-wide K tiles (M > 16), the kernel re-reads the group’s scale from its shared-me…
items.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #45000. With an FP8 block-quantized checkpoint, the dense Marlin kernel intermittently returns wrong GEMM results, which shows up as wrong greedy tokens. When a 128-wide group spans two 64-wide K tiles (M > 16), the kernel re-reads the group’s scale from its shared-memory stage slot on the second tile, but warp 0’s next `cp.async` can already have refilled that slot with the scale two groups ahead, with no barrier in between. A lagging warp then scales a whole K tile with the wrong group’s scale. Both zero-point loads have the same pattern. vLLM fixed this in vllm-project/

## Summary

When context compaction splits an episode into multiple training rows, `rollout/raw_reward` gives that episode extra weight. For example, four episodes with rewards `[1, 0, 0, 0]` report a mean of `0.25`. Splitting the first and last episodes into two rows each raises the logged mean to `0.3333`, even though the episode rewards are identical.

Compute the mean over episodes before data-parallel partitioning. Each episode contributes equally, including when its segments land on different ranks. In the example above, the logged mean stays at `0.25` after splitting.

items.title: Distributed optimizer: one FP32 main-grad conversion per bucket shard
items.author: sraman-rgb
items.summary: Fuses scattered BF16/FP16-to-FP32 main-gradient conversions per bucket shard into a single vectorized Triton kernel, cutting 23 launches to 1 and reducing conversion time ~3.6×.
items.body:
Add OptimizerConfig.fused_main_grad_copy (--fused-main-grad-copy, default off). With it, _copy_model_grads_to_main_grads groups this rank's BF16/FP16 grad shards into runs of adjacent shards of one grad buffer (normally one per bucket shard) and converts each run with one vectorized Triton kernel (megatron/core/fusions/fused_float_upcast.py) instead of one .float() per parameter. Each main grad is a view of its run's FP32 tensor; the conversion is exact, so the values are bit-identical. FP32 grads and the precision-aware optimizer are unchanged, and the path works under CUDA graph capture.

items.title: Single-pass fused router with compact route probs
items.author: sraman-rgb
items.summary: Fuses MoE router top-k selection, aux-loss scores, and token counts into a single Tensor Engine kernel with compact float32 probabilities to eliminate redundant casts during DeepEP/NCCL-EP training dispatch.
items.body: Add moe_router_fused_aux_scores (default off). For training steps with the 'deepep'/'ncclep' flex dispatcher and a router configuration TE's fused_topk_with_aux_loss_scores supports (sigmoid, 256 experts, top-8, optionally 8 groups / group top-4), the router computes the top-k, the aux-loss scores and both token counts (aux loss, expert bias) in one TE kernel and returns compact [num_tokens, topk] probs aligned with the dense int64 indices (float32 with expert TP 1, which removes the dispatcher's cast and its backward). The flex dispatcher and the DeepEP/NCCL-EP managers accept compact probs.

## Overview

`get_external_cache_hit_sources` works out which tier each offload hit token came from. vllm/v1/hisparse/binding.py, in resolve_hisparse_specs

vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_planning.py, in get_kv_cache_groups
vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_planning.py, in _get_packed_kv_cache_groups
ValueError: KV cache layout has not been resolved yet

items.title: [Perf] pooler: Avoid rebuilding pooled hidden states before scoring
items.author: AEGO-WRJ
items.summary: Setwise and multi-item scoring gather selected hidden-state rows into a contiguous tensor, split it into per-request views, then immediately concatenate the same views before applying the classification head. The concatenation allocates and copies a second com…
items.body:
## Motivation

Setwise and multi-item scoring gather selected hidden-state rows into a contiguous tensor, split it into per-request views, then immediately concatenate the same views before applying the classification head. The concatenation allocates and copies a second complete pooled buffer. For 32 requests with 64 selected rows each and hidden size 4096, that extra buffer is 16 MiB in FP16 or 32 MiB in FP32.

## Modifications

Keep the gathered tensor and request counts together until after scoring. Apply the same head to the same two-dimensional rows, then split scores and, when requested

items.title: [ROCm][Bugfix][Kimi-K3] Label the fused MLA fp8 outputs with the platform fp8 dtype
items.author: xaguilar-amd
items.summary: Fixes incorrect FP8 dtype labeling for fused MLA ops on ROCm gfx942 where e4m3fnuz outputs were mislabeled as e4m3fn, crashing Kimi-K3.1 DSpark inference.
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On gfx942 (MI325X), the Kimi-K3 fused MLA ops write e4m3fnuz, but their Python wrappers label the outputs `torch.float8_e4m3fn`. As a result, Kimi-K3.1 with the DSpark draft fails to start: AITER's MLA decode rejects the draft's query. This PR labels those buffers with `current_platform.fp8_dtype()` and relabels them to e4m3fn only at the op boundary.

Related: #66769, which Kimi-K3.1 needs to start on gfx942, and #67446, which fixes the separate 4 GiB KV view issue for the same draft. 

## Claims

- Kimi-K3.1-Pro with DSpark (`kv_cache_dtype: fp8`)

## Motivation

A rank's weight loader reads every checkpoint shard it needs through mmap. items.summary: uses fixed 32/32/32 block sizes for every M. For decode (M <= 16), most of the 32-row M tile is padding, and the narrow N tile issues small weight loads, so the kernel is limited by weight reads. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Overview

`awq_gemm_triton` uses fixed 32/32/32 block sizes for every M. For decode (M <= 16), most of the 32-row M tile is padding, and the narrow N tile issues small weight loads, so the kernel is limited by weight reads. This PR picks smaller-M / wider-N tiles when M <= 16 and leaves larger M unchanged.

## Claims

- For M <= 16, `awq_gemm_triton` uses `BLOCK_M=16`, `BLOCK_N=64`, `BLOCK_K=min(64, group_size)`.
- M > 16 keeps 32/32/32. Callers that pass explicit block sizes are unaffected.
- AWQ decode GEMM, Qwen2.5-Coder-14B-AWQ shapes, M=1, RX 9070 XT (gfx1201): **1.4–1.6x faster** pe

items.title: [Perf][ROCm] AWQ: keep awq_gemm for decode under torch.compile
items.author: adityaja-amd
items.summary: Under, the AWQ token-count heuristic in ( → dequantize + matmul, else ) is specialized once at compile time and reused for every batch size. As a result, decode (M=1) also takes the dequantize + matmul path.
items.body:
## Overview

Under `torch.compile`, the AWQ token-count heuristic in `AutoAWQLinearMethod.apply()` (`num_tokens >= 256` → dequantize + matmul, else `awq_gemm`) is specialized once at compile time and reused for every batch size. As a result, decode (M=1) also takes the dequantize + matmul path. This PR moves the dispatch into a registered custom op (`torch.ops.vllm.awq_linear`), so the heuristic is evaluated per call at runtime.

## Claims

- Decode now uses the fused `awq_gemm` kernel again, instead of `awq_dequantize` (which writes the full fp16 weight to memory) followed by a large GEMM.

items.title: [Fix] [AMD] kvcache: Write V with its own head size in reshape_and_cache_flash
items.author: tkarttunen
items.summary: assumes K and V have the same head size: the launcher takes and the kernel uses that size and for the V load, the V store and the V mask. When V is narrower than K, every V write reads past the token's V row and writes past the cache slot's V row.
items.body:
## Motivation

`reshape_and_cache_flash` assumes K and V have the same head size: the launcher takes `head_size = key.shape[2]` and the kernel uses that size and `BLOCK_D` for the V load, the V store and the V mask. When V is narrower than K, every V write reads past the token's V row and writes past the cache slot's V row.

items.body:
## Motivation

With DP attention, the breakable prefill CUDA graph, and decoder- plus encoder-SWA bounded replay on DeepSeek-V4, every DP rank must reach the same graph-or-eager decision for a prefill step. Otherwise one rank replays the graph while another runs the step eagerly, and their collectives no longer match.

The DP vote (`_local_prefill_cuda_graph_vote`) asks the backend's `vote_prefill_cuda_graph` whether the late-layer tail of the batch fits the in-graph tail block. That vote reads the raw `batch.extend_lens`. Later, the worker's `fold_encoder_swa_replay` prepends each prefix hit'

items.title: [Feat] sgl-router: credit a shared Mooncake HiCache L3 pool to every member worker
items.author: whn09
items.summary: With HiCache L3 on Mooncake Store, a page one worker writes to the pool can be loaded by every worker attached to the same pool. sgl-router's cache-aware routing credits only the worker that holds a page in its own KV events, so it keeps a prefix sticky to whi…
items.body:
## Motivation

With HiCache L3 on Mooncake Store (`--hicache-storage-backend mooncake`), a page one worker writes to the pool can be loaded by every worker attached to the same pool. sgl-router's cache-aware routing credits only the worker that holds a page in its own KV events, so it keeps a prefix sticky to whichever worker wrote it, even when a less loaded worker could load the same prefix from L3. The tree already has an `EXTERNAL` tier for "a shared / remote pool, e.g. Mooncake", but routing reads `prefix_depths`, which ignores tiers, and the engine emits no L3 events today (RFC #29709).

items.title: [vllm, rollout] fix: preserve the length stop reason in token outputs
items.author: yyDing1
items.summary: Today the vLLM rollout server reports both when generation stops naturally and when the output budget cuts it off. A caller translating this value to the Anthropic Messages API consequently sends for a truncated response, and the client can exit with work stil…
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Preserve vLLM's `finish_reason="length"` in `TokenOutput.stop_reason`. Today the vLLM rollout server reports `completed` both when generation stops naturally and when the output budget cuts it off. A caller translating this value to the Anthropic Messages API consequently sends `end_turn` for a truncated response, and the client can exit with work still in progress.

### Design and compatibility

Map vLLM's `stop` to `completed` and let `length` pass through the existing fallback. Callers can now return `max_tokens` to Anthropic clients. Abort still maps to `aborted`

## Motivation

`reduce_scatterv` and `all_gatherv` are used by variable-length DP attention and MoE communication paths, where ranks may process different numbers of tokens. `all_gatherv` gathers token data across ranks, while `reduce_scatterv` reduces partial outputs and scatters them back according to each rank's token count.

These operations currently require `PyNccl` and lack support for `non-PyNccl` backends such as `CNCL` for MLU platform. This PR adds a `torch.distributed` fallback when `PyNccl` is unavailable.

items.title: [Bugfix][Model] Use FP32 vision RoPE in Qwen3_VisionTransformer
items.author: ziywang50
items.summary: Qwen3/VisionTransformer RoPE cache and Q/K rotation now use FP32 instead of BF16, cutting HF↔vLLM vision L2 from ~0.2% to <0.001%.
items.body:
## Purpose

Related: #66070

HF's Qwen3.5 / Qwen3-VL vision tower computes RoPE frequencies, cos/sin and the Q/K rotation in FP32, then casts back. `Qwen3_VisionTransformer` builds its rotary cache with `get_rope(...)` without a dtype, so the cache takes the model's default dtype (BF16) and the angles are rounded before the rotation.

This PR makes `Qwen3_VisionTransformer.__init__`:
1. build the cache with `get_rope(..., dtype=torch.float32)`, and
2. set `enable_fp32_compute = True` on each block's `apply_rotary_emb`, so Q/K are rotated in FP32 and cast back to the model dtype.

items.body:
Custom Megatron model providers still need changes to slime's built-in HF loader/exporter registries before they can load a checkpoint and sync weights to rollout engines. This adds two optional import-path callbacks to keep model-specific tensor mappings outside slime:

- `--custom-hf-weight-loader-path`: maps a Megatron parameter/buffer name to its HF tensor. Checkpoint detection honors the callback; loading retains the shared padding, sharding, shape validation and dtype/device copy.
- `--custom-hf-weight-converter-path`: maps a Megatron tensor to HF named tensors after shared normalization

### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8675.

The Minerva scorer keeps only the text after the last `=`, so `x=2, y=3`

assignments during normalization so the scorer compares both values.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Searched for [similar PRs](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+math_dapo). #8450 covers Markdown extraction, and #8124 covers boxed-answer fallback.

### What does this PR do?

Restore bounded layered LoRA collection for FSDP1 layouts with flattened parameters or independently wrapped adapter leaves. The collector currently checks local parameter names, passes local keys to PEFT, and recursively summons nested units. These behaviors can drop adapters or export a nested `_flat_param`. An empty result then triggers a full-model CPU summon on every FSDP1 rank, defeating the memory bound requested by layered collection.

Initialize FSDP1 from its real root, recognize original flat-parameter names and leaf prefixes, normalize parameter ownership

items.title: Create the HF export directory on every writing rank, and fail if it is not shared
items.author: zhanglei-amd
items.summary: Rank 0 creates the --save-hf directory and copies the non-weight files of --hf-checkpoint into it, then the shard writers on other nodes open files in it. On NFS a client that looked the path up before rank 0 created it can keep that negative lookup cached for…
items.body:
Rank 0 creates the --save-hf directory and copies the non-weight files of --hf-checkpoint into it, then the
shard writers on other nodes open files in it. On NFS a client that looked the path up before rank 0 created it

The SGLang patch stack adds TokenizerManager.post_process_weights, which always takes the writer side of
model_update_lock. During an in-place pause_generation the requests in flight keep the reader side, so the call
waits for requests that cannot finish while the engine is paused, and the weight update hangs. SGLang's own update
calls avoid this: update_weights_from_disk skips the writer lock while paused, and begin_weight_update and
end_weight_update go through _weight_update_session_call, which does the same. slime pauses the engines in place
whenever a weight update does not flush the cach

## What does this PR do?

With MFSDP v2, DSA models fail at the first optimizer step. For models with a DSA indexer, the optimizer computes the indexer and non-indexer gradient norms on every step for logging. The base `get_dsa_split_grad_norms` goes through `get_grad_norm_fp32`, which requires all DTensor gradients to share one mesh, but the non-indexer half mixes dense and expert gradients. `FullyShardedOptimizer` now computes both norms the way its `get_grad_norm` already does, from each gradient's own layout.

A DeepSeek-V4 Pro proxy on 64 GB200 with MFSDP v2 now runs past the first step.

items.title: [#22150][fix] Register RPC response futures before sending requests
items.author: itsrayeedscodespace
items.summary: A regular RPC reply can reach while is still awaiting the transport send. The response future is currently registered only after sending, so the reader discards that reply and the caller waits indefinitely with the default timeout.
items.body:
## Description

Fixes #22150.

A regular RPC reply can reach `_handle_regular_response` while `_call_async` is still awaiting the transport send. The response future is currently registered only after sending, so the reader discards that reply and the caller waits indefinitely with the default timeout. Remote errors can be lost in the same way.

Register the future under the existing admission/close lock before sending. Include the send in the existing `try/finally` so send failures and caller cancellation remove the registration. Fire-and-forget calls still send without allocating a response

items.title: [reward] fix: compare prime_code call-based outputs as plain builtins
items.author: Aarav500
items.summary: In, call-based tests compared the generated function's return value with. The generated code controls that object, so a subclass of or whose always returns got full reward on every call-based task.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8656. In `prime_code`, call-based tests compared the generated function's return value with `output == expected`. The generated code controls that object, so a subclass of `int` or `list` whose `__eq__` always returns `True` got full reward on every call-based task. Swapping the operands doesn't help, because Python tries a subclass's reflected `__eq__` first.

This adds `_to_builtin()` in `prime_code/testing_util.py` and applies it to the output right after the existing `json.dumps(output)` call. It rebuilds the value from plain `None`/`bool`/`int`/`float

items.body:
## Problem and behavior

Checkpoint participants each own one GPU, but Ray's default first barrier can enroll every visible GPU and its rendezvous key contains the local ordinal. The engine now owns a device-bound NCCLGroup specialization with a single-device barrier and a logical group key shared across masked/shared ordinal layouts. Allocation, executor-thread broadcast, synchronization and destruction use the engine device. Ordinary Ray groups retain their behavior, and duplicate ownership/topology checks remain. Delta transfers reuse this group and device without changing the wire protocol

## Problem

With `--cuda-graph-impl full_iteration`, `FullCudaGraphWrapper` captures the whole forward/backward, including `forward_step` / `get_batch`. The per-iteration sequence statistics therefore split into two halves that behave differently under replay:

- `_seqlen_stats_in_iteration` is a device tensor, so `update_seqlen_stats_from_cu_seqlens`'s `+=` is captured and replayed;
- `_seqlen_stats_active` is Python state, set only while capturing.

Once `consume_seqlen_stats_in_iteration` drains the capture iteration and clears the flag, every later replayed iteration reports `(None, None)`

items.title: [fsdp] feat: project LM head only for response tokens
items.author: hxw12219
items.summary: Adds an opt-in FSDP engine option, (default ). RL losses read values only at response tokens, but the engine projects every packed token through the LM head.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Adds an opt-in FSDP engine option, `response_only_lm_head` (default `false`). RL losses read values only at response tokens, but the engine projects every packed token through the LM head. With the option on, the engine passes the packed rows that predict response tokens to the model as Transformers' `logits_to_keep`, so the eager and fused LM heads project only those rows. The values at response tokens are unchanged.

## Summary

Fixes #2519.

`_apply_model_patch` chained `git apply --verbose`, `git apply --verbose --reject` and `patch --batch --fuzz=5 -p1 -i` with `||` and no reset in between. When the first `git apply` failed on one hunk, `--reject` applied the other hunks and exited non-zero. `patch --batch` then treated those hunks as a reversed patch, undid them, and could exit 0. The grader reported the patch as applied while the model's changes were gone, so a correct fix scored 0. The issue's standalone script reproduces this with GNU patch 2.8.1.

- Drop the `git apply --reject` tier. It exits 0 on

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Allow colocated NPU rollouts to explicitly select vLLM-Ascend's native IPC loading lifecycle. The trainer packs bounded byte buffers, exports a fresh IPC reference for each nonempty bucket, and waits for the worker to finish consuming that bucket. Leaving the option unset preserves the existing CUDA/ROCm, shared-memory and delta dispatch paths.

This is part 1 of a three-PR series: IPC, HCCL, then whole-stream reload.

items.title: [ray] fix: prevent master port races during worker startup
items.author: SeptPonts
items.summary: Prevent during Ray worker startup caused by the gap between selecting a master port and binding PyTorch's TCPStore. Previously, probed a free port with a temporary socket, closed it, and passed the port to workers.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Prevent `EADDRINUSE` during Ray worker startup caused by the gap between selecting a master port and binding PyTorch's TCPStore.

Previously, `RayWorkerGroup` probed a free port with a temporary socket, closed it, and passed the port to workers. Another process could claim that port before rank zero initialized its process group.

Rank zero now binds and retains the actual TCPStore before invoking the user worker constructor. It publishes the bound endpoint before that constructor can block waiting for peers, allowing the driver to start the remaining ranks.

items.title: Fix math_dapo Minerva extraction for markdown-decorated answers
items.author: siddhant-rajhans
items.summary: The existing regex captures the markers as part of the answer, so correct answers score -1.0. Fixes #8449 ## Root cause The Minerva answer pattern matches the literal "Answer" and captures everything after the colon to end of line.
items.body:
## Bug

Models commonly wrap the Minerva `Answer:` label in markdown bold/italic (`**Answer:** 42`, `Answer: **42**`, `**Answer:**\n\n42`). The existing regex captures the `*` markers as part of the answer, so correct answers score -1.0.

Fixes #8449

## Root cause

The Minerva answer pattern `(?i)Answer\s*:\s*([^\n]+)` matches the literal "Answer" and captures everything after the colon to end of line. When models decorate with markdown:

| Input | Extracted | After normalize | Score |
|---|---|---|---|
| `**Answer:** 42` | `** 42` | `**42` | -1.0 |
| `Answer: **42**` | `**42**` | `**42**` |

## Problem

For `k3` and `low_var_kl`, `compute_approx_kl` evaluates `exp(x) - 1 - x`, where `x = log_probs_base - log_probs`. This expression is nonnegative in real arithmetic, but subtracting 1 from a float32 exponential can erase the small KL term or make it negative when the policies are close.

With valid finite log-probabilities near -0.1, I reproduced a value of -1.4901161e-8 where an 80-digit reference gives 4.9986626e-11. The helper feeds the reported KL term and configured KL loss/reward paths; the Search-R1 example selects `low_var_kl` with a nonzero KL-loss coefficient.

items.author: 0z5a
items.summary: After that, the acceptance length is ~1.0 and rollout is slower than with speculative decoding off. How it happens: - slime's colocated sender calls with, and.
items.body:
## Problem

With `--sglang-speculative-algorithm DFLASH` and a colocated rollout engine, the first weight sync silently overwrites the DFLASH draft with target weights. After that, the acceptance length is ~1.0 and rollout is slower than with speculative decoding off.

- slime's colocated sender calls `update_weights_from_tensor` with `serialized_named_tensors`, `load_format="flattened_bucket"` and `weight_version`. It sets neither `selector` nor `disable_draft_model`.

items.title: fix(data): give uniform reward groups exactly zero advantage
items.author: saloni-garg
items.summary: When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about …
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In `_post_process_rewards` the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about an ulp instead of zero. With std normalization on, the residue is then divided by its own std, which turns it into a small nonzero advantage shared by the whole group.

Small reproduction on current main (a group of 16 rollouts that all scored 0.3, `grpo` with `grpo_std_normalization`):

-
discussion: The nonzero advantages for uniform fractional rewards reproduce on `main`. I ran the grouped-reward tests at `0063710` on CPU with PyTorch 2.13.0: uniform groups produce exact zeros, and the mixed-group and nonfinite-reward cases pass too.
Thank you for checking, and for reproducing it on main as well. Glad the tests hold up on your side too. Happy to run anything else you would like to see here.

items.author: ActuallyEdward
items.summary: Duplicate IDs accumulate in FP32. Preserve top-p replay and non-SC execution paths.
items.body:

## Summary

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.
items.body:
## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.
items.body:
## Background

Locally managed SGLang servers are polled through `/health_generate` before rollout initialization can continue.

## Problem

The startup poll had neither a request timeout nor an overall deadline. A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.

## Solution

- Add `--sglang-server-startup-timeout` with a positive finite value and a conservative 600-second default.
- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.
- Reject readiness

## Background

A custom generation function may return multiple training segments for one input. `generate_and_rm_group` preserves that result as `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

When `group_rm` is enabled, the nested result was passed directly to the group reward function and trace helper. Those paths expect `list[Sample]`, so fan-out generation and group rewards could not be combined.

## Solution

- Flatten one level before tracing and invoking the group reward function.
- Assign returned rewards to the same leaves in stable fan-out order.

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ

## Background

## Problem

The done callback inspected only the outer list. An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.

## Solution

- Snapshot the flat input group before generation can mutate it.
- Inspect one-level fan-out leaves for `Sample.Status.ABORTED`.
- Requeue the pristine flat snapshot

## Approach

- A one-character label that is a valid option letter is no longer added t

Training and evaluation launch rollout tasks concurrently at three levels: samples within a rollout group, rollout groups within a training batch, and samples within an evaluation batch.

## Fix

At each concurrency boundary, cancel unfinished sibling tasks and wait for their cleanup before re-raising

items.title: require --ref-load when KL is enabled instead of crashing with a TypeError
items.author: rootkiller6788
items.summary: Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slimevalidateargs with, because it stat'd args.refload before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.
items.body:
Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slime_validate_args with `TypeError: _path_exists: path should be string, bytes, os.PathLike or integer, not NoneType`, because it stat'd args.ref_load before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.

This adds the same guard: ref_load unset now raises a ValueError telling the user to pass --ref-load, and a ref_load that points nowhere still raises the original FileNotFoundError. Two unit tests cover both cases.

items.title: fix: preserve equals in extra environment values
items.author: imshunsuke
items.summary: For example: was parsed as: This corrupts padded or otherwise -containing environment values. JSON input handling and the existing fallback tokenization remain unchanged.
items.body:
## Summary

- Preserve `=` characters after the first separator in the space-separated `extra_env_vars` fallback parser.
- Add regression coverage to the always-on CPU test matrix.

## Problem

`_parse_extra_env_vars` split each assignment on every `=` and then kept only the second component. For example:

`TOKEN=abc== END=ok`

was parsed as:

`{"TOKEN": "abc", "END": "ok"}`

This corrupts padded or otherwise `=`-containing environment values.

## Change

Use `split("=", 1)` so only the key/value separator is consumed. JSON input handling and the existing fallback tokenization remain unchanged

## Background

In the agentic rollout path, each agent turn sends a request to SGLang through the SGLang router. When a request is cancelled or hits the client-side read timeout, Slime must explicitly abort the corresponding SGLang request to release its scheduler slot and KV-cache resources.

`sglang_url` points to the SGLang router address, but the router does not expose or forward the `/abort_request` endpoint.

## Problem

Thanks to @kkyyxhll for catching in #2319 that SGLang ignores `sampling_params.temperature` when it computes input/prefill log-probs. OPD samples from the temperature-scaled student distribution `p_T`, so leaving the teacher at its implicit default computes `KL(p_T || q_1)`, not the matched-temperature objective `KL(p_T || q_T)`.

Passing the rollout temperature through sampling parameters is currently a no-op, while pinning it to `1.0` only makes the mismatched behavior explicit. Supporting the real-temperature case requires changing the SGLang input-logprob path.

items.body:
## Summary
- Expose `--advantage-estimator dapo` as a preset over the existing GRPO implementation.
- Enable Clip-Higher, token-level loss, the default dynamic-sampling filter, and Soft Overlong defaults.
- Add `--soft-overlong-cache` and apply its length penalty before existing reward normalization.
- Document the preset in English and Chinese.

## Design
DAPO does not add a second advantage, loss, or normalization path. Argument validation expands it to the existing GRPO primitives; the only new rollout behavior is Soft Overlong reward shaping.

- Replace the previous local checkpoint only after the copy completes.
